sorting_rule.description: sorting_year = the BC/AD year of the first tier that has a non-null year_bc_ad. Events use chronologies[]. People use dates.birth[] when a tier 1–4 birth year is stored. A person who has a dates.reign slot and no tier-ranked birth year uses the reign-start year (year_bc_ad already stored on dates.reign); sorting_basis.slot is then reign_start. Within ussher-jones, for that reign-start choice, the 23rd edition (2026) governs over an older Jones edition when both print a year. The first matching entry within a tier is used otherwise; for split years (2348/2347) the start year is used. No year is derived. Secondary display chronologies (bible, masoretic-genealogy, jordan, josephus, Clonmacnoise, Raleigh, Herodotus, Cory, Shuckford, Hales, and CFAH paper_text) never set sorting_year. Exception, pending owner decision: where no tier gives a year, the Generations curriculum supplies a PROVISIONAL sort (tier "provisional"; see A8 in docs/OPEN-QUESTIONS-FOR-KEVIN.md). Kevin's ruling, 2026-10-28 (open question M3).

tiers.select: cfah entry with cfah_basis = table1_baseline (CFAH-1 Table 1)
ussher-jones entry (Floyd Nolen Jones). On a reign-start sort, the 23rd edition (2026) governs over an older Jones edition when both print a year.

sorting_rule.fallbacks: People with no tier birth year and a dates.reign slot: sorting_year is the tier 1–4 reign-start year (slot reign_start) before any provisional fallback. If no tier yields a year: tier "derived" (sorting_year copied from the record named in derived_from; events only by convention) or tier "none" (sorting_year null; people only). Tier "provisional" (records with no tier 1-4 year only): sorting_year = the first dated generations entry (events: chronologies[]; people: dates.birth[]); badged as provisional.

chronologies.name: Chronological Framework of Ancient History
chronologies.description: Primary sorting chronology. A planned 20-paper series in Answers Research Journal (CFAH-1 to CFAH-6 published as of 2026-10-17) that harmonises durations from ancient chroniclers with Ussher's biblical chronology as modified by Floyd Nolan Jones ("Ussher-Jones"). Only dates read directly in the ARJ papers are entered; every CFAH date carries paper + section citation. Each dated cfah entry carries cfah_basis: "anchor_point" (dates the papers derive/triangulate, e.g. AP-29, AP-30) or "table1_baseline" (CFAH-1 Table 1, the Ussher-Jones biblical baseline the authors adopt). These are sort tiers 1 and 2.
chronologies.year_conventions: Dates given in Julian BC; split years written as 2348/2347 (year_bc_ad = -2348, year_bc_ad_end = -2347). CFAH papers do not use AM numbering in their anchor points; year_am left null unless the paper states it.

chronologies.name: Ussher-Jones (Floyd Nolen Jones, The Chronology of the Old Testament)
chronologies.description: Floyd Nolen Jones's refinement of Ussher (The Chronology of the Old Testament: A Return to the Basics). The figures that set a sort come from the most recent publication, the 23rd edition (Master Books, 2026), Appendix F, where that edition prints a year for the same event. Older citations (Chart No. 1, 1993; 15th edition, 2002) stay on the record. Where the 23rd edition prints a different year, that year governs the ussher-jones entry and the sort, and the older figure stays in a note. CFAH treats Jones as its biblical baseline (CFAH-1 Table 1), but here Jones is a separate chronology so his own statements are cited directly. It is the third sort tier: after a CFAH anchor point and after CFAH-1 Table 1, and before Ussher. Jones sets the sort for any record that has no CFAH year, in the Old Testament, the intertestamental period, and the New Testament. A Jones row sets that sort only when it names the same event. A row that names a different event is display only. A person with no tier 1–4 birth year, and with a dates.reign slot, sorts on the reign-start year Jones already prints there; the 23rd edition governs that year over an older Jones edition. Years are stored only as Jones prints them. An AM figure is never converted into a BC or AD year.
chronologies.year_conventions: Creation = 0 AM = 4004 BC; Jones states "any BC number added to its corresponding AM counterpart will always yield the value 4004" (15th ed. 2002, Chart Five discussion, p. 110). That rule is documented here but NOT used to convert AM-only figures; year_bc_ad is filled only where Jones prints the BC year.

anchors.citation: Jones, Chart No. 1 "Creation to Jesus Christ" (© 1993)
Jones, Chart No. 1 "Creation to Jesus Christ" (© 1993); Chronology of the Old Testament (15th ed., 2002), Chart One §B, p. 26

open_questions: Kevin ruled (2026-10-27) that the 23rd edition (2026) governs a ussher-jones year where it differs from the 15th edition (2002) or the charts. The older figure stays in a note. The free 21st-edition URL (floydnolenjonesministries.com/files/135786316.pdf) returned 404 and was not used.
The ministry page's link for Chart 6 "Creation to Creator" points to the Chart 5C file (same URL), so Chart 6 could not be read.

Jones charts are largely images in the 2002 PDF, so patriarch death years on those chart images were not readable as text. Appendix F of the 23rd edition prints AM and BC/AD. Where the 15th-edition compendium printed an AM and no BC, that AM-only entry is kept beside the 23rd-edition entry. No AM figure is converted.

Kevin ruled (2026-10-27) that Jones sets the sort for the Old Testament, the intertestamental period, and the New Testament wherever no CFAH anchor point or CFAH-1 Table 1 year is present. A CFAH year still wins. A Jones row sets the sort only for the same event (docs/OPEN-QUESTIONS-FOR-KEVIN.md, section M).
Reign-start years do not sort a king or a judge who has no birth year. That question stays open (docs/OPEN-QUESTIONS-FOR-KEVIN.md, M3). No validator change.

chronologies.name: Ussher, Annals of the World (1650/1658)
chronologies.description: Archbishop James Ussher's Annales Veteris Testamenti (1650), English edition 1658. Gives Anno Mundi (AM), Julian Period (JP) and BC years for each entry.
chronologies.year_conventions: AM 1 = 710 JP = 4004 BC (Creation began at the evening preceding 23 October 4004 BC, Julian). Ussher's year runs autumn to autumn, so one AM year straddles two BC years; Ussher's printed BC heading is used for year_bc_ad. E.g. AM 1656 (Flood begins) is headed 2349 BC and AM 1657 (Noah leaves the Ark) is headed 2348 BC.

chronologies.name: James B. Jordan, Biblical Chronology (Biblical Horizons / ICE, 1989-1997) and Studies in Biblical Chronology Nos. 2-3 (2001)
chronologies.description: SECONDARY DISPLAY CHRONOLOGY - never used for sorting_year (not one of the four sort tiers). James B. Jordan's monthly newsletter Biblical Chronology (Institute for Christian Economics / Biblical Horizons, 1989-1997). Framework: six 24-hour creation days, no gaps in Genesis 5 or 11, Masoretic numbers (rejects the LXX and the "second Cainan"); Flood AM 1656; Arphaxad AM 1658 ("two years after the Flood"); Abram born AM 2008 (Terah 130, from Gen 11:26 + Acts 7:4) - the same as Ussher and 60 years later than plain Gen 11:26 arithmetic (1948); the 430 years of Ex 12:40 counted from Abram's entry into Canaan (AM 2083), so the Exodus is AM 2513 (same as Ussher/Jones); Judges partly overlapping, 480 years to the Temple foundation in Solomon's 4th year, AM 2993 (one year later than Ussher/Jones 2992), completed AM 3000, dedicated (he assumes) AM 3014 (Ussher: 3001); kings of Judah as the controlling "Adamic chronology" (rejects Thiele and the conventional Assyrian synchronisms); fall of Jerusalem c. AM 3425; decree of Cyrus c. AM 3474; Daniel's 70 weeks taken as 490 literal years from Cyrus, which REJECTS the Ptolemaic Persian chronology and shortens the post-exilic period by about 80 years; crucifixion AM 3960 and, "if this happened in A.D. 30", the fall of Jerusalem in A.D. 70 = AM 4000. Consequence: Jordan's B.C. dates (his "SBC", strictest Biblical chronology, first set out in BC 5:8, Dec. 1993) run about 74-75 years later than Ussher/CFAH for the same events (Creation 3930 B.C., Flood 2274, Abram 1922, Exodus 1417, Temple begun 937), while his AM figures mostly match Ussher. Later issues (Daniel series 1995) date the Persian period with conventional B.C. years (e.g. Cyrus 538 B.C.), so his B.C. usage is not uniform. JUDGES PERIOD: Jordan set out two schemes. (1) BC 3:7-3:8 (July-Aug. 1991): the 300 years of Judges 11:26 end at Jephthah's victory, AM 2853. (2) From Creation to Solomon (Studies in Biblical Chronology No. 2, Oct. 2001), ch. 11: the 300 years run 2560-2860 and end when Ammon took the villages, so his judges dates move 26 years later (Jephthah 2879, Eli begins 2841, Saul 2909, David born 2919, Samuel dies 2946). Both are recorded on the judges records, 2001 first. Jordan's 1980s books (Law of the Covenant 1984, Judges 1985, Sociology of the Church 1986, Through New Eyes 1988, Covenant Sequence 1989, and the Christianity and Civilization symposia) give intervals at most; see data/jordan-dates-extract.md.
chronologies.year_conventions: Anno Mundi counted from Adam's creation as year 0 ("0 - Adam created"; Seth 130), written "AM 1656", "A.M. 2008", or month/day/year as "2/17/1656". His year sometimes runs from spring (Pentateuch plague calendar, "1st Month (March-April 2513)") and sometimes turns in the 7th month (wilderness narrative, BC 6:8 §18). year_bc_ad is filled only where Jordan prints a B.C. year, which is almost always his SBC figure; the note says so. Nothing is converted between AM and B.C. Many of his dates carry "?" or "c." or are called "arbitrary"/"aesthetic"; those use precision "conjectural".

chronologies.name: Biblical statements (direct Scripture data)
chronologies.description: Dates/durations stated explicitly in Scripture (relative dates such as "in the six hundredth year of Noah's life, in the second month, the seventeenth day"). The Bible is the infallible standard; this chronology records the text's own statements without conversion.
chronologies.year_conventions: date holds the scriptural wording/paraphrase; year_am filled only when the verse itself fixes it relative to a stated life (otherwise null); year_bc_ad always null.

chronologies.name: Masoretic Text genealogy arithmetic (Genesis 5 & 11)
chronologies.description: Straight arithmetic on the Masoretic/KJV figures of Genesis 5 and 11 with no external calibration: each birth = father's birth + father's age at begetting; each death = birth + lifespan.
chronologies.year_conventions: Anno Mundi counted as completed years from the creation of Adam (Adam created AM 0; Seth born AM 130 because "Adam lived an hundred and thirty years, and begat... Seth", Gen 5:3). The Flood falls in AM 1656 (Noah born AM 1056; Flood in his 600th year, Gen 7:6, 7:11). year_bc_ad is always null (the text gives no BC anchor).

chronologies.name: Josephus (Whiston translation)
chronologies.description: Chronological statements in Josephus, Antiquities of the Jews (Whiston translation). Josephus's figures for the antediluvians largely follow LXX-type numbers in the received text; Whiston's brackets give Masoretic corrections.
chronologies.year_conventions: Years from Adam as Josephus states them (stored in year_am); no BC conversion.

anchors.citation: Josephus, Antiquities I.3.3 (Whiston)

chronologies.name: Raleigh, The History of the World (1614/1617)
chronologies.description: SECONDARY DISPLAY CHRONOLOGY. It never sets sorting_year and is not one of the four sort tiers. Sir Walter Raleigh's History of the World (1st ed. 1614; primary text the 1617 issue, EEBO-TCP A10357 / STC 20638 / ESTC S112960; 11th ed. 1736 as secondary reading copy), Books I–V from Creation to 130 BC. Entries quote the 1617 text and keep his yeere of the World in year_am. year_bc_ad stays null. The site shows a display-only italic BC or AD year from his Creation in 4032 BC, as AM 1656 (2377 BC). That year is not a printed year, and it does not set the sort, a standby placement, a span, or a tier.
chronologies.year_conventions: Yeere of the World as Raleigh prints it (year_am). A table year is stored only when the Julian Period exceeds that yeere by 682 (To the Reader, sig. 781a). His example of Jehoshaphat, Julian 3774 and World 3092, is on sig. 780b. year_bc_ad stays null. Display only: his first yeere of the World (AM 1) is taken as 4032 BC, so a year before Christ is 4033 minus AM, and a year of our Lord is AM minus 4032 once AM is 4033 or later. There is no year 0. Each end of a range is converted on its own. An illegible figure, a two-figure yeere that is not fully legible, or a missing figure is flagged and not derived. An optional stored derived_bc_ad must match that formula and carry derived_from raleigh-creation-4032-bc. It is never a sort. Under the portal's Julian Period (JP 1 = 4713 BC), his own +682 puts AM 1 at JP 683 = 4031 BC (sig. 781b). Kevin decided on 2026-10-28 (G11) to keep 4032 BC. The 4031 BC reading is recorded and is not the formula used. The text is the 1617 issue, EEBO-TCP A10357, in sources/raleigh/ (EarlyPrint unadorned). The anchors below are those 1617 readings. The 1736 edition stays in sources as a reading copy and is not cited on these anchors.

anchors.date: The generall Floud was in the yeere of the World 1656.
anchors.citation: Raleigh, The History of the World (1617, EEBO-TCP A10357), Book I, ch. VII, §III, sig. 96a. The chronological table (sig. 782a) prints "The Floud." at the same year.

The same section's "An. mundi 2008 dil. 352. natus Abraham, Eus. Aug. de Ciuit. Dei" names Eusebius and Augustine and is not this anchor.

Raleigh, The History of the World (1617, EEBO-TCP A10357), Chronological Table, sig. 784a. Book II, ch. IIII, §I, sig. 184a also prints the Passover in the yeere of the World 2514. Sig. 174a prints "or after our account, 2513," which is not this anchor.

The same signature, at World 2994, prints "Salomon beganne to build the Temple 480. yeeres compleat after the deliuerance out of Aegypt." That sentence was not attached to an event. This pass does not create events.

chronologies.name: Anno Mundi Chronology Studies (compilation of Jordan's system)
chronologies.description: SECONDARY DISPLAY CHRONOLOGY. It never sets sorting_year and is not one of the four sort tiers. It is kept separate from "jordan", which holds Jordan's own published figures. A 14-page set of charts that compiles James B. Jordan's Anno Mundi system from Creation to Solomon (Judges as in his 2001 From Creation to Solomon), with an A.M./B.C. table running to A.D. 70. The owner confirmed it as an accurate compilation (2026-10-18). Its B.C. column is the compiler's own: Creation 4010 B.C., so B.C. = 4010 − AM through the Temple (3000 AM = 1010 B.C.). This is about 80 years earlier than Jordan's SBC (3930) and 6 years earlier than Ussher (4004). Known slips against Scripture and Jordan: Enosh dies 1130 (should be 1140); Arphaxad dies 2093 at 435 (should be 2096 at 438). It corrects Jordan's Mahalalel 396 to 395. Jephthah 2878 vs Jordan 2879; Moses dies 2553 vs Jordan 2554; Jacob dies 2315 vs Jordan 2313 (Jordan's slip). Each entry notes agreement or difference with Jordan's own figure.
chronologies.year_conventions: AM as printed (year_am). B.C. (year_bc_ad) only where the compilation prints a B.C. year (pp. 3 and 11). Nothing is converted. Its AM has a year 0 ("There is a “0” year in A.M.", p. 13).

chronologies.name: Generations curriculum (Swanson et al.)
chronologies.description: SECONDARY DISPLAY CHRONOLOGY. It is never one of the four sort tiers and never overrides them. Dates come from five Generations curriculum books (Taking Africa / Europe / Asia / the World for Jesus; Preparing the World for Jesus), each with a book and PDF page citation. Records that no tier reaches (mostly AD church and missions history) take a PROVISIONAL sort year from the first Generations date: sorting_basis tier "provisional", badged on the site and pending the owner's decision (docs/OPEN-QUESTIONS-FOR-KEVIN.md, A8). Where a record already has a tier 1–4 date, Generations is display-only and any disagreement is flagged.
chronologies.year_conventions: Dates are as printed: BC/AD as the book gives them, with circa and approximate qualifiers kept. year_bc_ad is filled only from a printed year; nothing is converted or inferred. Precision "approximate" marks circa/about/around; a bare "AD" or "BC" is taken from the sentence or the chapter context and stated in the note when the book omits it.

chronologies.name: Herodotus, The Histories (tr. George Rawlinson)
chronologies.description: SECONDARY DISPLAY CHRONOLOGY. It is never a sort tier and never sets or overrides a sort year. Each entry quotes Herodotus's own words (Rawlinson's translation) with Book.chapter and the page of the Roman Roads Media etext (2013), the edition CFAH cites, and links to the same passage in the public-domain Wikisource text. Herodotus gives reign lengths, intervals and synchronisms rather than BC years, so entries carry no BC year. A BC year worked out from his figures appears only in the note, labelled DERIVED, with its arithmetic and its anchor (a CFAH anchor point, or CFAH-3's 450 BC for his visit to Egypt). Agreements and conflicts with CFAH, Ussher and Generations are listed in data/herodotus-dates-extract.md.
chronologies.year_conventions: No year conversion. Entries keep year_bc_ad and year_am null and precision "unknown"; the date field is the quoted statement. Derived BC years in notes are marked DERIVED and are never presented as Herodotus's figures.

chronologies.name: Joe Morecraft III, A Christian Survey of World History from Creation to the Reformation
chronologies.description: SECONDARY DISPLAY CHRONOLOGY. It is never a sort tier and never sets or overrides the sort of a record that has a CFAH, Ussher–Jones, Ussher or Generations date. Records created by the Morecraft import, which no other chronology dates, sort PROVISIONALLY by their Morecraft year until a tier 1–4 date is added (open question F1). Each entry gives the date as printed, with the printed page and the PDF page of the owner's private scanned copy. The book is copyrighted: only dates, citations and short notes in our own words are kept. Agreements and conflicts are listed in data/morecraft-dates-extract.md.
chronologies.year_conventions: year_bc_ad is the year as printed (negative = BC; no year 0). Ranges as printed go in year_bc_ad/year_bc_ad_end; for a person's birth and death slots a printed life span is split into its two years. "Approximately", "around" and "probably" are kept as precision approximate/conjectural. No years are derived.

chronologies.name: Cory, Ancient Fragments (1876, ed. E. Richmond Hodges)
chronologies.description: SECONDARY DISPLAY CHRONOLOGY. It is never a sort tier and never sets or overrides a sort year. Each entry quotes the 1876 Hodges edition of Cory's Ancient Fragments (London: Reeves & Turner), with the printed page and the fragment chain (for example Manetho, ap. Syncellus and Eusebius). Reign lengths stay in the quotation (years, months, days, sari, neri and sossi). A year of the world printed by Eratosthenes or in the editor's Africanus summary stays in the quotation. Entries carry no BC year and no stored Anno Mundi: year_bc_ad, year_bc_ad_end and year_am stay null. A parenthetical such as "(b.c. 878)" is kept inside the quotation and is not a sort year. A product worked from the text's own definitions appears only in the note, labelled DERIVED. A sum we add up is labelled "Our check (not a figure of the text)" and is not a year. Pass 1 is the Tyrian Annals, the antediluvian kings, and the Chaldean and Assyrian lists. Pass 2 adds Manetho's dynasties, Josephus's Manetho, the Old Chronicle, Eratosthenes, Diodorus's Egyptian canon, the editor's Africanus table, and the other dated fragments in the volume. Editorial introductions and footnotes that are not fragments stay out. Agreements and conflicts are listed in data/cory-dates-extract.md.
chronologies.year_conventions: No year conversion. Entries keep year_bc_ad, year_bc_ad_end and year_am null and precision "unknown"; the date field is the quoted statement. Durations and printed years of the world stay in that quotation (years, months, days, sari, neri, sossi, Anno Mundi). A parenthetical BC year printed in the edition is not stored as year_bc_ad. Anno Mundi is not converted to BC. Derived products in notes are marked DERIVED, and a sum we compute is marked as our check. Neither is presented as the edition's figure.

chronologies.name: Shuckford, The Sacred and Profane History of the World Connected (1819, ed. James Creighton)
chronologies.description: SECONDARY DISPLAY CHRONOLOGY. It is never a sort tier and never sets or overrides a sort year. Each entry is a date read in volume 1 of the fifth edition, revised by James Creighton (London: William Baynes, 1819). Shuckford counts by the year of the world. year_am is that printed Anno Mundi. year_bc_ad is set only when the page prints “before Christ” or “before our Saviour”. Anno Mundi is not converted to BC. A figure he sets out and does not adopt is left out of the record and listed in the extract. This pass is volume 1 only. Agreements and conflicts are listed in data/shuckford-dates-extract.md.
chronologies.year_conventions: No conversion of Anno Mundi to BC. year_am is the printed year of the world. A range he prints uses year_am and year_am_end. year_bc_ad is negative and is used only for a “years before Christ” or “years before our Saviour” figure printed on the page. “About” and “it is thought” are precision approximate. A subtracted year is labelled DERIVED in the note and is not stored.

chronologies.name: Hales, A New Analysis of Chronology (1830, 2nd ed.)
chronologies.description: SECONDARY DISPLAY CHRONOLOGY. It is never a sort tier and never sets or overrides a sort year. Each entry is a line from his own tables in the second edition, corrected and improved (London: C. J. G. & F. Rivington, 1830): the Synopsis of the Chronology in volume II, Periods I–VII, from the Creation through Nehemiah’s reform, and Table XI in volume I from the Creation through the Era of Nabonassar. He prints a B.C. column, and that figure is year_bc_ad. year_am stays null. A parenthesis is the Hebrew age he prints beside the longer age he adopts, and it is not stored as a second year. His Creation is B.C. 5411, which conflicts with the Masoretic creation year. Scripture governs. This pass is partial. Agreements and conflicts are listed in data/hales-dates-extract.md.
chronologies.year_conventions: He prints B.C. years in these tables. year_bc_ad is that column (negative). year_am is null: Anno Mundi is not printed in these rows and is not converted. Reign lengths and braced subtotals stay in the quotation. A parenthesis is the Hebrew age he does not adopt. A day and month he prints use precision day. “Our check” notes confirm a total he already prints and are not stored.
